vintagekinematics:block-handbooktext-vin:
The Primitive Sieve is a copper tier hand crank worker. Feed it gravel, sand, soil, or any vanilla pannable material and let the shaft do the panning for you.

IO
Input: top or side feed face. Output: bottom or the opposite side, so it sits cleanly on top of storage. If the sieve faces north/south, side input is east and side output is west. If it faces east/west, side input is south and side output is north.

Yield rolls match hand panning, but it processes whole blocks instead of hand panning 1/8 of a block at a time. The early reward is throughput, especially once geared up.

The Kinetic Quern grinds vanilla quern recipes and turns rock grit into finer dust that sieves at higher yield with no dead rolls.

IO
IO is relative to the direction you faced when placing it. Input is from the left side or top. Output is from the right side or bottom. Example: facing north while placing gives west input and east output.

Output faces push into adjacent inventories, including chests, vessels, funnels, vanilla chutes, and hoppers. A belt on the right side also works when it is moving away from the quern.

The Crusher Basin holds the item being crushed by a crusher head above it. It crushes raw rock and stones into grit, and graded ore blocks from poor through bountiful into enriched ore nuggets. Bronze crusher heads work through iron tier materials and can make crushed bauxite for tier 1 and tier 2 refractory mix. Iron crusher heads handle every crusher tier. For ilmenite, crush ore chunks into nuggets, then crush nuggets into crushed ilmenite for tier 3 refractory mix.

IO
IO is relative to the direction you faced when placing it. Input is from the left side or top. Output is from the right side or bottom. Output faces push into adjacent inventories, including chests, vessels, funnels, vanilla chutes, and hoppers. A belt on the right side also works when it is moving away from the basin.

Belts move items while powered. Right click with another belt to chain parallel shaft endpoints. Right click an empty handed belt to scoop every carried item on the chain into your inventory.

A belt automatically picks up from a machine output side it runs past, deposits into a machine input side, and feeds a chest, vessel, or other storage placed at its end. Machine output faces also push into adjacent inventories, vanilla chutes, hoppers, and funnels. Belt output requires the belt to move away from the machine output face.

Items stop at a solid block in their path and wait until the exit clears or a side funnel pulls them off.

A funnel pulls items from the block directly above it and ejects out the face it points at. To drain a chest or vessel, place the funnel below the storage and face it toward the target. Open the funnel to set whitelist, blacklist, exact, or fuzzy filtering.

Copper funnels are 16x slower and have fewer filter slots. Iron funnels are faster and carry more filtering capacity.

Funnels are best when you need active pulling or filters. Machine output faces can also push directly into adjacent inventories, including vanilla chutes and hoppers.

The Kinetic Sieve processes crushed rock, grit, dust, and vanilla pannable materials to recover sand, ore nuggets, gems, and rock-specific drops.

IO
Input is from the top or the side feed face of any drum segment. Output is from the bottom or the opposite side. If the drum faces north/south, side input is east and side output is west. If it faces east/west, side input is south and side output is north.

The Kinetic Sawmill cuts logs into planks, shafts, sticks, or cogwheel sections while powered. Choose the mode in its GUI.

IO
Input is from the top or the side feed face chosen when placed. Output is from the bottom or the opposite side. Attach belts and funnels to non shaft faces so log input does not fight the shaft connection.

The Kinetic Extractor squeezes seeds, fruit, and similar organic inputs into oils, juices, and solid byproducts while powered.

IO
Item input is from the top or side feed face. Solid output is from the bottom. If the shaft axis is east/west, side input is south. If the shaft axis is north/south, side input is east. Liquid output stays in the internal buffer for collection.

The Kinetic Forge Press is a fueled hot metal press. It heats metal, consumes rotation, and stamps plates, bloom output, dies, brackets, casings, pistons, collars, flanges, and alloy stock. After your first vanilla bloomery batch, it can smelt 20 limonite, hematite, or magnetite nuggets into an iron bloom, then refine that bloom into an iron ingot. It can also melt quartz, olivine, and quartz crystals into glass.

IO
Metal and fuel input come from the top or side feed face. Output exits from the bottom or opposite side. If the shaft axis is east/west, side input is south and side output is north. If the shaft axis is north/south, side input is east and side output is west.

A powered Kinetic Bellows beside the press raises chamber heat faster and hotter, and reduces the pain of larger heated batches. Bloom smelting and glass melting are high heat recipes tuned for a two bellows press.

T3 lining
Sneak right click the press with 24 fired tier 3 refractory bricks to install the high heat lining. The lining plus powered bellows reaches titanium heat and marks the T3 entry point.

The Kinetic Bellows helps the Kinetic Forge Press and vanilla firepits. Place it beside the press with the nozzle aimed at the multiblock to raise chamber heat faster and hotter. Point the nozzle at a firepit to accelerate burn and heating work.

The in-world tooltip reports whether the bellows is active and what target it is affecting.

The Kinetic Mixer is a two block powered mixer. Drive the upper cog cell with kinetic rotation; the lower basin does the mixing work. Its GUI has a 3x3 input grid and a 3x3 output grid.

IO
Solid inputs enter from the lower side feed face only. Output exits from the bottom or the opposite lower side. If placed on the east/west axis, side input is south and side output is north. If placed on the north/south axis, side input is east and side output is west. Slaked lime can be poured in by bucket or supplied from an adjacent liquid container.

Recipes
Mortar: put 2 rock grit and 1 sawdust in the mixer, then supply 1 L slaked lime to make 4 mortar.
Richer mortar: put 2 rock dust and 1 sawdust in the mixer, then supply 1 L slaked lime to make 6 mortar.
It also automates dry blends such as plaster, blasting powder, raw refractory brick mix, and high fertility soil.

The Kinetic Bore is a heavy industrial drill. Feed it encased shafts and rotation; it descends one block per cycle and leaves a 3x3 shaft behind it.

IO
Load drill rods in the GUI. Mined output is exposed from the upper back center face, opposite the front/shaft side. Put a funnel, chest, chute, hopper, or belt moving away from the bore against that back output face to drain it.

The Treadwheel is the sustained player powered source of the crank era. Stand inside the wheel and press movement to run in place; hold backward to reverse direction. Use it when hand crank bursts are too short or when an early crusher or sieve needs steadier power.

The Flywheel stores rotational energy while a treadwheel, counterweight drive, coal motor, or other strong source is spinning its input side. The dark shaft is input; the lighter shaft is output. Right click any connected flywheel to toggle the whole bank between charge mode and release mode.

In charge mode only the input side connects and it is a 1024 SU consumer at 16 RPM. In release mode only the output side connects and it becomes a 1024 SU source at 16 RPM for up to 180 stored seconds. Stored charge holds while the flywheel is installed in a valid, non-overstressed kinetic network. Sneak right click to set bank burst output to 1x, 2x, 4x, or 8x. Burst output multiplies SU and drains stored time at the same multiplier, so it spends stored work faster without creating extra work. Gear high RPM charging before the input side; gear high RPM output after the output side.

For forge press storage with 16x burst output, see the Reinforced Flywheel.

The Reinforced Flywheel is a forge press era 1x3x3 kinetic buffer with metal rim mass and bearing parts. Place the bottom middle cell; the shaft line is one block above it. The wood shaft is input and the metal shaft is output.

In charge mode only the input side connects and it is a 10240 SU consumer at 16 RPM. In release mode only the output side connects and it becomes a 10240 SU source at 16 RPM for up to 900 stored seconds. Stored charge holds while the bank is installed in a valid, non-overstressed kinetic network. Sneak right click to set bank burst output from 1x up to 16x. Burst output multiplies SU and drains stored time at the same multiplier. Connected same axis flywheels toggle and configure together as one bank.

For the smaller crank era version, see the Flywheel.

The Reinforced Chest is a 32 slot post forge storage block. It costs a normal chest plus pressed bands, a shaft collar, planks, and a kinetic alloy plate, so it is a compact workshop upgrade rather than a cheap early chest replacement.

Use it as a direct output buffer for machines, belts, funnels, vanilla chutes, and hoppers. For one item type in high volume, use a Reinforced Crate.

The Double Reinforced Chest is a 1x2 reinforced storage block with 70 slots. Craft it from two Reinforced Chests when a workshop buffer needs more mixed-item space without becoming a bulk crate.

Either half opens the same inventory. Machine outputs, belts, funnels, vanilla chutes, and hoppers can use it like other VK storage.

The Reinforced Crate is a 64 stack industrial crate for one item type. The first item inserted locks the contents, and the crate rejects other item types until emptied. It upgrades a vanilla crate with pressed casings, pressed bands, and kinetic alloy plates.

Use it for high volume output like grit, dust, planks, ore, stone, or repeated machine products. Adjacent machine outputs, belts, funnels, vanilla chutes, and hoppers can feed it as long as they are sending the stored item type.

The Kinetic Clutch is an inline shaft switch. When engaged it behaves like a normal shaft. When open it splits the kinetic network at that block, stopping rotation from crossing the clutch.

Right click to toggle it. Use it to isolate machines, stop gantries, or prevent two sources from conflicting.

The Kinetic Reverser is an inline shaft that can flip rotation across itself. In straight mode it passes rotation like a normal shaft. In reverse mode the chosen output side is inverted, so rotation crossing the block reverses direction.

Right click to toggle between straight and reversed mode. Place it facing the side you want to behave as the reversed output.

The Kinetic Activator consumes rotation and activates the block in front of it. Right click the activator to cycle modes: repeat while rotating, once until stopped, once per rotation direction, or pulse burst. Sneak right click cycles the activation delay: instant, 500 ms, 1000 ms, 1500 ms, 2000 ms, or 5000 ms. Ctrl right click cycles burst pulses: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, or 16.

Repeat mode waits that delay between activations. The one shot modes wait that delay after rotation starts, then activate once until stopped or once for that rotation direction. Pulse burst mode fires the configured number of pulses each time rotation starts, or when rotation direction changes. Blocks can opt into precise activator behavior through the VK kinetic activator API. As a first supported target, it can wind a Hand Crank in the direction of the activator's rotation.

Server configs can blacklist unsafe activator targets by block code, block class, block entity class, or entityClass name.

The Gantry Shaft is a powered track for constrained moving contraptions. Build a straight line of gantry shafts on one axis, then place a Gantry Carriage onto the line. Powering the shaft moves any assembled carriage along the track until it reaches the end, then it stops and can reverse when shaft rotation reverses.

This is the first contraption prototype, so keep builds modest and test them before moving anything valuable.

The Gantry Carriage attaches to a Gantry Shaft and carries a bound block assembly along that straight track. Place it on top of horizontal gantry shafts, or on any horizontal side of a vertical gantry shaft. Use a Mechanical Binder to select two corners of the assembly, then right click the carriage to assign the selection.

Right click the carriage to assemble or restore the contraption. Sneak right click cycles its placement mode.
vintagekinematics:item-handbooktext-vint: The Mechanical Binder selects the blocks a Gantry Carriage will carry. Left click two block corners to draw a box, then right click a Gantry Carriage to assign that selection. Only connected blocks are kept in the assembly, so floating blocks are discarded.

Make this billet in the Kinetic Mixer from one iron ingot and two charcoal powder. Heat it in an upgraded Kinetic Forge Press and run the Blister Steel operation to make blister steel, then refine that into steel.
vintagekinematics:block-handbooktext-vin: The Counterweight Drive stores hand work as a timed burst of kinetic power. Right click to wind the weight, then sneak-right click to release the stored drive. It is useful for batches where you want the machine to run without standing at it the whole time.

The bronze crusher is the early driven head of a crusher pair. Mount it above a Crusher Basin and feed it with a shaft. It turns raw rock and stones into grit, crushes ore blocks through iron tier materials into enriched ore nuggets, and crushes bauxite into crushed bauxite for tier 1 and tier 2 refractory mix.

Steel tier and harder pulverizer materials require the iron crusher.

The iron crusher is the faster version of the crusher head. Mount it above a Crusher Basin and feed it with a shaft; it handles every crusher and vanilla pulverizer tier at 50% higher speed than bronze. It is the VK route for high tier ilmenite processing after the Forge Press part chain: ore chunks crush into nuggets, and nuggets crush into powder for tier 3 refractory mix.

vintagekinematics:vkguide-progression-ov:
Vintage Kinematics Progression

Vintage Kinematics is a separate kinetic system with its own shafts, stress units, gearboxes, and machines. Vanilla windmills and water wheels can still feed VK through the bridge behavior described in Kinetics for Dummies, but the VK machine ladder is its own progression path.

The short path
1. Build a hand crank, shaft, and primitive sieve.
2. Use the primitive sieve to process whole gravel, sand, and soil blocks through vanilla panning drops. The early reward is manual powered throughput: whole blocks per cycle instead of hand panning 1/8 of a block at a time.
3. Add a treadwheel or counterweight drive when hand crank bursts are too short.
4. At bronze, build a bronze crusher over a crusher basin to turn rock into grit.
5. At iron, build the Kinetic Forge Press. It heats and stamps metal into plates, bloom output, dies, brackets, casings, pistons, collars, flanges, and alloy stock.
6. Use Forge Press parts to build post forge machines: full kinetic sieve, iron crusher, sawmill, friction igniter, iron funnel, powered tools, and reinforced packs.
7. Stamp a pressed casing and piston head for the coal motor. This is the bridge from player driven machines to sustained fuel power.

Why the ladder matters
VK machines are meant to pay back the vanilla climb without skipping it. Copper gives your first kinetic throughput upgrade; true unattended automation starts only once you drive VK with vanilla wind/water power or later coal power. Bronze gives rock crushing. Iron gives hot stamped machine parts. Post forge parts unlock better machines and player rewards. The coal motor then turns that workshop into a sustained factory.

First target
If you are new, do not start with the coal motor. Start with a crank powered primitive sieve on top of a chest. When that throughput setup works, add stronger crank era power, then crushing, then the forge press.
vintagekinematics:vkguide-crank-era-text:
Crank Era: Your First Working Line

The first real VK build is small: a hand crank, one shaft, and a primitive sieve. Put the sieve on top of a chest, feed pannable gravel, sand, or soil from the top, then wind the crank. The primitive sieve uses vanilla panning drops, so the reward is throughput: it processes whole blocks instead of hand panning 1/8 of a block at a time, and gearing can make it much faster.

Primitive Sieve
The primitive sieve is the copper tier hook. It accepts vanilla pannable blocks only, not rock grit or dust. Output goes downward and out the opposite side, so a chest below is the easiest setup. This is still manual powered before vanilla power or the coal motor, but it can run very fast when you gear the sieve up.

More powerful crank era sources
The hand crank is the starter source for short bursts. The stronger machines in this era are the treadwheel and counterweight drive; use them when the primitive sieve or early crusher needs longer runs, higher stress capacity, or less constant clicking.
- Treadwheel: the sustained player powered source of the crank era. Stand inside and move to provide steadier, stronger power than a hand crank.
- Counterweight Drive: the stored work source of the crank era. Wind it by hand, then sneak right click to release drive time for batches without standing at the machine.

Bronze crushing bridge
Once you reach bronze, place a bronze crusher above a crusher basin. The crusher turns rock and stones into grit, and ore blocks into enriched ore pieces. Feed that grit into the full kinetic sieve later for rocktype keyed drops. The primitive sieve remains for vanilla pannables; the full sieve owns the industrial rock loop.

Other early workers
The kinetic quern handles quern work and can grind grit into richer dust for the full sieve. The kinetic extractor is the organic press lane for seeds, fruit, and similar recipes; it is not the metal forming press. Belts and copper funnels move items once your line has more than one machine.
vintagekinematics:vkguide-forge-press-er:
Forge Press Era: Stamped Parts

The Kinetic Forge Press is the iron tier boundary. It burns fuel, heats the workpiece, and uses rotation to stamp hot metal. This is VK's hot metal former: it makes metal plates, smelts iron ore nuggets into blooms after your first vanilla bloomery batch, refines iron blooms, and produces reusable die parts for later machines.

What goes in
The Forge Press has separate slots for metal input, fuel, die, and outputs. Heat matters: the chamber warms gradually, and recipes only advance when the workpiece is hot enough and the kinetic network is powered. Plates, bloom smelting, and iron bloom refining do not need a die. Brackets, casings, piston heads, shaft collars, pipe flanges, bearing blanks, industrial plates, drill heads, and many other parts use reusable dies.

Use Bellows for heat
A powered Kinetic Bellows beside the Forge Press raises chamber heat faster and hotter. Two bellows are expected for bloom smelting. A bellows nozzle can also point at a vanilla firepit to speed burn and heating work. Use it when forge press batches feel fuel bound or when you want faster firepit heating in the same workshop.

T3 lining
After the iron crusher unlocks ilmenite processing, make fired tier 3 refractory bricks and sneak right click 24 of them onto the Forge Press. The upgraded lining plus powered bellows reaches titanium heat. This is the official T3 entry point and enables titanium ingots and the Titanium Powered Drill.

Post forge machine unlocks
Stamped parts turn iron into machinery instead of just plates.
- Machine brackets unlock machines such as the full kinetic sieve, iron crusher, sawmill, and friction igniter.
- Pipe flanges upgrade logistics through the iron funnel.
- Pressed casings and piston heads are the coal motor bridge.
- Kinetic alloy plates and kinetic alloy rods unlock player rewards such as the reinforced backpack and powered drill.

Full rock processing
After the Forge Press, the full kinetic sieve becomes the industrial partner to the crusher and quern. Crusher grit gives rocktype keyed drops. Quern dust is slower to prepare but richer to sift. The iron crusher is faster than the bronze crusher, so the same rock line becomes more useful instead of obsolete.
vintagekinematics:vkguide-coal-motor-era:
Coal Motor Bridge

The coal motor is the first sustained VK fuel source. It is intentionally post forge: build the Forge Press first, stamp a pressed casing and piston head, then assemble the motor with the other required parts. There is no all vanilla shortcut into fuel power.

Why it matters
Hand crank, treadwheel, and counterweight drive all spend player attention. The coal motor spends fuel instead. Once it is running, your crusher, sieve, quern, sawmill, bellows, extractor, belts, and funnels can work as a real workshop instead of a batch of hand powered stations.

Good first uses
- Keep a crusher, quern, and full sieve moving for rock to metal processing.
- Run a bellows beside the Forge Press during long stamping batches.
- Power belts and funnels so input and output buffers do not stall machines.
- Use the sawmill to turn logs into planks, shafts, sticks, and cogwheel sections while the rest of the line runs.

Player rewards after the press
The coal motor is not the only post forge goal. A reinforced backpack gives a practical storage upgrade, and a powered drill gives fueled mining with no durability loss while fueled. These use kinetic alloy parts, drill heads, and powered assemblies from the forge press chain.

After coal power
The current heavy machine endpoint is the Kinetic Bore, gated by deliberate industrial Forge Press parts such as steel industrial plates and rough bearing blanks. Longer term coal era machines will expand fuel, alloy, and heavy material processing, but the current practical climb is: post forge workshop -> coal motor -> sustained processing -> heavy drilling.
vintagekinematics:vkguide-kineticsfordum:
Vintage Kinematics
If it spins, it works. If it doesn't spin, check your shafts.

This guide covers the basics: how power flows, how to redirect and gear it, and how to move items between machines.

The Basics: RPM and SU
Every kinetic network has two numbers. RPM is rotation speed (signed: positive or negative direction). SU is stress, measured as capacity available versus capacity consumed. If consumers want more SU than sources provide, the network overstresses and stops. If two sources try to drive one network at different RPMs, the network conflicts and stops.

Power Sources
VK source paths include: the hand crank (rightmouse to spin), the treadwheel (stand inside and move), the counterweight drive (wind and release stored drive), and the coal motor (feed it coal), plus any vanilla mechanical-power network attached directly to a VK shaft. Place a VK shaft next to a vanilla axle, windmill rotor, or angled gear face on the same axis and VK reads its RPM and torque automatically. More sails and more wind mean more SU.

Carrying Power
A line of shafts on the same axis transmits power without ratio change. To turn a corner, use a gearbox: it accepts a shaft input on one face and drives a perpendicular output. To change ratio, mesh a small cogwheel against a large cogwheel: small driving large is a speed down with more torque headroom; large driving small is a speed up with less. Cogs sit on the same axis as the shaft they ride; the gear contact happens at the rim.

Item Logistics
A belt runs between two shaft endpoints on the same axis and conveys items along its length. Place a funnel at the input or output: a funnel always pulls from the block directly above it and pushes into the block on the side it is facing (north, east, south, or west). This means you can route items sideways out of a chest into a belt, into a machine's input face, or back into another container, just by aiming the funnel the right way when you place it. Funnels can also sit directly above a belt to drop items onto it, or alongside a belt facing inward to push items onto it. Compatible with vanilla chests, vessels, baskets, and most modded storage blocks. Each funnel has a filter slot with whitelist, blacklist, and fuzzy modes. Iron funnels move items faster than copper.

A belt that ends or runs alongside a machine can feed mapped input faces. Machine output faces push into adjacent inventories, funnels, vanilla chutes, hoppers, and belts moving away from the output face. Every machine declares which faces are inputs and which are outputs; see Machine IO or the machine's own handbook entry before routing logistics.

Machines
VK machines expose explicit input and output faces for automation. Many use top/input side and bottom/opposite side IO, while the quern and crusher basin use placement relative left to right IO. Each consumer also needs its driving face on the correct shaft axis. Open the GUI to see input, output, and progress.
- Kinetic quern: grinds via vanilla quern recipes.
- Crusher with a basin: crushes ores and rocks; the basin holds output and pushes to adjacent funnels, chests, chutes, hoppers, or belts moving away from output.
- Kinetic sieve: auto-pans gravel, sand, and crushed rock. Uses vanilla panningDrops so any pannable material from other mods works.
- Sawmill: cuts logs into planks and boards.
- Kinetic Extractor: extracts liquids and byproducts from organic inputs.
- Kinetic bore: multiblock drill that descends through stone and retracts on demand.
- Kinetic igniter: spark source for fueled blocks.

Your First Build
Start small: a hand crank driving a primitive sieve through a single shaft. Wind the crank, watch the sieve work. Then experiment with gearing: mesh a small cogwheel against a large cogwheel between the crank and the sieve. Try both directions: small driving large, then large driving small. See how fast you can make the sieve run before something gives. This is the whole mod in miniature: a source, a shaft, a gear stage, a consumer. Every later build is just more of the same.

Troubleshooting
Check the in-world tooltip on any shaft or machine for the live RPM and SU readout. If a machine sits idle, look at that readout first.
- Overstressed: SU demand exceeds capacity. Add another source, remove a consumer, or gear down to lower the RPM (consumer SU scales with RPM).
- Conflicted: two sources are pushing different RPMs into the same network. Disconnect one, or split the line with a vanilla clutch or brake.
- RPM zero, no overstress: a shaft segment is broken between source and consumer, or the source itself is stopped (low wind, no fuel, idle crank).

Build small, test as you go, and grow outward from a known-working source.
vintagekinematics:vkguide-machine-io-tex:
Machine IO

VK machines expose named input and output faces. Inputs accept items from funnels and belts moving toward the input face. Outputs push into adjacent inventories, funnels, vanilla chutes, hoppers, and belts moving away from the output face.

Quern and Crusher Basin
These use placement relative left to right IO.

top input
v
left input -> [machine] -> right output
v
bottom output

If you faced north when placing the quern or basin, west is input and east is output. Top is also input. Bottom is also output.

Primitive Sieve and Kinetic Sieve
Input: top or side feed face. Output: bottom or opposite side. If the sieve faces north/south, side input is east and side output is west. If it faces east/west, side input is south and side output is north.

Sawmill
Input: top or the side feed face chosen when placed. Output: bottom or the opposite side. Use the non shaft faces for item IO.

Extractor
Input: top or side feed face. Solid output: bottom. Liquid output stays in the internal liquid buffer for collection.

Forge Press and Mixer
Input: top or side feed face. Output: bottom or opposite side. With an east/west shaft axis, side input is south and side output is north. With a north/south shaft axis, side input is east and side output is west.

Kinetic Bore
Load drill rods in the GUI. Mined output drains from the upper back center face, opposite the front/shaft side.

Chutes and hoppers
Vanilla chutes and hoppers work on VK output faces because the machine pushes output into adjacent inventories. They still do not pull from VK input slots by themselves; use funnels or belts for active feeding and filtering.
